name: Question 1
problem: Which integral expression gives the arc length of the curve $f(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{t},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩$ from $t=-1$ to $t=1?$
worked_solution:
First, we find ${f}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{f}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{t},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{f}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+({e}^{t})^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+{e}^{2t}+{cos}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+2({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}‖{f}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+2}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Which integral expression gives the arc length of the curve f(t)=⟨cos⁡t+sin⁡t,et,sin⁡t−cos⁡t⟩ from t=−1 to t=1?

a
2∫−11et+2dt
b
∫−11e2t+1dt
c
∫−112et+1dt
d
∫−11e2t+2dt
e
2∫−112e2t+1dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find f′(t) and ‖f′(t)‖: f′(t)=⟨ddt(cos⁡t+sin⁡t),ddt(et),ddt(sin⁡t−cos⁡t)⟩=⟨cos⁡t−sin⁡t,et,cos⁡t+sin⁡t⟩‖f′(t)‖=(cos⁡t−sin⁡t)2+(et)2+(cos⁡t+sin⁡t)2=cos2⁡t−2cos⁡tsin⁡t+sin2⁡t+e2t+cos2⁡t+2cos⁡tsin⁡t+sin2⁡t=e2t+2(cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t)=e2t+2

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is L=∫−11‖f′(t)‖dt=∫−11e2t+2dt.
